articles.title: Kelly Krauskopf stepping down as Indiana Fever team president
articles.summary: Krauskopf started with Pacers Sports & Entertainment in 1999.
articles.body:
Kelly Krauskopf, who has served as president of basketball and business operations for the Indiana Fever since 2024, announced Friday that she is stepping down from her role.

"It has been an honor and a privilege to help build and steward the Indiana Fever with the support and trust of Herb Simon," Krauskopf said in a statement. "I am deeply grateful for the opportunities, relationships, and shared accomplishments that have shaped my time with this organization. The Fever is poised for an exciting future, and I am proud to have helped lay the foundation for its continued growth and success. I will always cherish my time with Pacers Sports and Entertainment and the people who made it so meaningful."

The 64-year-old has been part of Pacers Sports & Entertainment since 1999 when the Fever joined the WNBA. As the team's president and general manager until 2017, she helped the franchise make 13 playoff appearances and three WNBA Finals berths, which included a title in 2012.

In 2018, Krauskopf was named assistant GM of the Indiana Pacers and became the first woman to hold an executive basketball management role in NBA history.

After six years on the NBA side of the organization, Krauskopf returned to the Fever as president of basketball and business operations in 2024. One year later, the team reached the WNBA semifinals. In 2026, they were back in the postseason and improved their win total for the fourth straight season.

After her collegiate playing career at Texas A&M, Krauskopf was assistant commissioner of the Southwest Conference before joining the WNBA as the league's first director of operations when it started in 1996 . She has also been a part of three USA Basketball women's national team selection committees for multiple Olympic cycles.

articles.title: Why the Hawks are a rare NBA road favorite worth backing against the rebuilding Hornets
articles.summary: The Atlanta Hawks face the Charlotte Hornets with Jalen Johnson leading a revamped roster, while Brandon Miller tries to carry a depleted squad.
articles.body: The NBA is just a few days old and we've already seen two teams blow 20-point leads. That happens more often than you'd probably imagine, and this year I'm making a point to live bet on the team that is losing big. Last night the 76ers looked awful, but they came back in the second half of the game and covered the short spread. I'm sure it will happen somewhere today as well. There are a ton of great games to choose from, but I've got my eye on the Hawks and Hornets game. The Atlanta Hawks are one of the teams that have a bit of excitement behind them coming into this year. They revamped their roster quite a bit over the past few years, but now it seems like they have decided to build their team around Jalen Johnson. It also helps that they have two really good defenders - Nickeil Alexander-Walker and Dyson Daniels. The team moved on from Trae Young last year, who was a facilitator and scorer for them, but also a parking cone on defense, and it never seemed like the team worked with him. This team is now a little more athletic and younger, but still grounded with a couple of key veterans like CJ McCollum. In their opening game against the Magic, I was most impressed with their shot selection. As a team, they shot 50% from the field and 40% from deep. You really can't expect that to happen consistently, but they did create the good shots. Defensively, they really weren't impressive. They still gave up 125 points to the Magic, which is a lot for an Orlando team that isn't known for being offensively efficient. The Charlotte Hornets remain one of those teams that I really can't understand. They have been terrible for years, and the one time they sniffed success, they decided it was time to trade away their (arguably) best player. They sent LaMelo Ball over to the Timberwolves, but that's probably because they have Coby White, and they seem to want to invest in Kon Knueppel. Unfortunately for them, Knueppel is out with an injury right now, so the team is missing a major player. In their first game, they unveiled their new-look roster and beat the Brooklyn Nets on the road. This team is comprised of multiple role players, but right now, their biggest semblance of a star is Brandon Miller. No offense to Miller, but if he is responsible for leading the team for multiple games, you're probably asking for trouble. I do think the Hornets are going to be hovering around the play-in positioning for the postseason, but I really don't think they've improved from last year. They do play at home tomorrow, against a tougher opponent, so this could be a trap spot, but I'm going to take them on the moneyline at -135. articles.title: ‘Getting a ring before Luka ‘ – NBA Fans excited for Dalton Knecht as he signs two-way contract with New York Knicks
articles.summary: Former LA Lakers player Dalton Knecht has found a new home as the New York Knicks signed him to a two-way contract just days after the Purple and Gold outfit...
articles.body:
Former LA Lakers player Dalton Knecht has found a new home as the New York Knicks signed him to a two-way contract just days after the Purple and Gold outfit waived him.

The former Tennessee player was the 17th pick in the 2024 NBA Draft. He had a solid rookie season, but after a poor second year and a disappointing preseason, the Lakers decided to waive him from their final roster.

However, just days later, Knecht has been picked by the Knicks, who waived Kevin McCullar Jr. to make room for the former Lakers player.

McCullar was one of the players on the Knicks roster who was given the ring on opening night. He had impressive performances for the team, but the franchise decided to give Knecht a chance to prove his talent to the rest of the league.

In the preseason, Knecht scored 11 points against the Golden State Warriors in one game and went scoreless in two others. His form has been in decline since the Lakers decided to trade him away, and a deal was even in place with the Charlotte Hornets. But after it collapsed due to Mark Williams' failed medical, Knecht had to return to Los Angeles.

After that debacle, he has failed to find himself, which is why a change in environment could prove to be massive for him.

Fans react to Dalton Knecht signing with the New York Knicks

Knecht had a top rookie season. In a game against the Utah Jazz, he scored 37 points, draining 9 three-pointers, a record for a rookie in the NBA.

Despite his performances, the team included him in a trade package for Mark Williams; from then on, he failed to replicate the talent that was on display until February of 2025.

There is evidence that Knecht is a tremendous shooter. While it has not been on display in a long time, the Knicks are playing a gamble that can be fruitful.

Fans were excited to hear that the team had added another promising talent to the roster.

"Dalton getting a ring before Luka," said one fan. An account named Real App on X added: "Knicks going back-to-back confirmed."

Someone also stated: "Let shooters shoot……. We are wishing the best for this ex Laker."

"This is a good swing for a player with shooting upside. If it works out, Knicks get an elite shooter. If it doesn't, who cares. Good buy low from the Knicks," a fan opined.

An account user remarked: "Good luck Dalton! Hopefully getting recruited by the champs is the confidence boost he needs."

Knecht has a chance to do something special with the Knicks and even convert his two-way into a standard NBA contract. The team has a lot of special players who are selfless. He will have to adapt to this, as it is the only way he can succeed in the organisation.

articles.title: Knicks Plan to Give 275 Employees NBA Championship Rings After Phishing Email 'Mistake'
articles.summary: In the wake of a report from The Athletic's Joe Vardon detailing a phishing test in the form of an email sent to various  Madison Square Garden employees about receiving a 2025-26 NBA championship ring from the New York Knicks, the club is now planning to give out rings.
articles.body:
In the wake of a report from The Athletic's Joe Vardon detailing a phishing test in the form of an email sent to various Madison Square Garden employees about receiving a 2025-26 NBA championship ring from the New York Knicks, the club is now planning to give out rings.

Per Stefan Bondy of the New York Post , the Knicks are planning to give 275 championship rings to members of the organization after acknowledging the "unfortunate mistake" of using the emails as a simulation of a phishing test.

"The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers," an MSG spokesman told Bondy. "MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack. Using the rings as a lure to gain employees attention was an unfortunate mistake."

According to Vardon's report, the Knicks were not planning to give out rings to "many longtime" MSG employees. The group included some who work in the business operations department for the Knicks.

Vardon also included text of the phishing email sent by the Knicks to various MSG employees:

"Congratulations, your Employee Championship Ring is here," the email read.

"(Employee name), this one is on the house. MSG is issuing a complimentary employee championship ring. The same jeweler, the same craftsmanship, personalized with your name. No cost to you.

"There are two designs to choose from: Championship Gold and Garden Classic. Reserve the one you want below."

Vardon noted the email was designed to be a "fake-out" and people who clicked the link were "forced to attend a mandatory cybersecurity class" because Knicks governor James Dolan had growing concerns about cybersecurity.

The Knicks handed out rings to celebrate their victory in the 2026 NBA Finals on Tuesday prior to their season-opening game against the Philadelphia 76ers.

However, some of the boxes given out to assistant coaches on head coach Mike Brown's staff did not open theirs to show off the ring because the box was empty.

Vardon noted assistants learned earlier in the day they would not be receiving their rings on Tuesday.

According to Bondy, top Knicks assistant coaches Chris Jent, Rick Brunson and Brendan O'Connor are expected to receive their rings "shortly" and the other assistants will "eventually" get theirs.

The MSG spokesman told Bondy the 275 rings will go to players, coaches, employees and other members of the Knicks family. The combined value of all the rings will total more than $3.7 million.

All of the players who were on the Knicks roster and in attendance at Madison Square Garden on Tuesday got their rings. Team president Leon Rose and executive vice president - senior basketball advisor William Wesley also received theirs during the pregame ceremony.

articles.title: Former LSU men's basketball coach Dale Brown, program's all-time wins leader, dies at 90
articles.summary: Brown coached the Tigers to two Final Fours and 13 NCAA tournament berths during his 25 seasons in Baton Rouge.
articles.body:
Former LSU men's basketball coach Dale Brown died Friday at the age of 90. Brown's family confirmed his death in a statement issued to multiple outlets and the LSU program.

Brown coached the Tigers for 25 seasons from 1972-97, compiling a record of 448-301. His win total is the highest in LSU men's basketball history and his 238 conference wins rank second behind Kentucky's Adolph Rupp in SEC history.

LSU's best season under Brown was the 1980-81 campaign, when the Tigers finished with a 31-5 record, a first-place standing in the SEC and a trip to the Final Four.

During Brown's tenure, LSU won four SEC regular-season titles and one conference tournament championship. His teams earned 13 NCAA tournament berths and advanced to two Final Fours.

Brown's 1985-86 team was the first No. 11 seed to ever reach the Final Four , defeating No. 6 Purdue, No. 3 Memphis State, No. 2 Georgia Tech and No. 1 Kentucky in the Southeast region on its way to the national semifinals. The Tigers lost in the Final Four to Louisville, the No. 2 seed out of the West.

LSU nearly made a third Final Four in the 1987 NCAA tournament, losing to eventual national champion Indiana 78-77 in the Elite Eight.

"We have lost the most loving and most loved man any of us has ever known. Dale Brown always put others first," Brown's family said in a statement. "He always led with the heart. He was always a great humanitarian before anything else." "Dale long ago fell in love with Louisiana," the statement added. "And the people of Louisiana loved him right back. We are forever grateful for that."

"We have lost the most loving and most loved man any of us has ever known. Dale Brown always put others first," Brown's family said in a statement. "He always led with the heart. He was always a great humanitarian before anything else."

"Dale long ago fell in love with Louisiana," the statement added. "And the people of Louisiana loved him right back. We are forever grateful for that."

Brown's death comes days after he received the 2027 John R. Wooden Legends of Coaching Award from the Los Angeles Athletic Club. The award will be presented during a ceremony in April in Los Angeles.

"I will always remember Dale for his enthusiasm," the legendary UCLA coach once said of Brown. "There are those who say he is a put-on — they just can't believe that he can be what he professes. But I never questioned that. He amazed me because there is a lot more depth to the man. He was much more than a basketball coach."

The star players Brown coached in Baton Rouge include Hall of Famer Shaquille O'Neal, Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf (then Chris Jackson), John "Hot Rod" Williams and Rudy Macklin. Macklin, O'Neal and Abdul-Rauf rank second, sixth and eighth, respectively, among LSU's all-time leading scorers .

articles.title: NBA Scout Questions If Celtics' Jayson Tatum Is 'Same Guy' After Recovery from Achilles Injury
articles.summary: As the very early takeaways from the 2026-27 NBA season come pouring in, one thing people in the league are keeping an eye on is Jayson Tatum as he still rounds into form following his Achilles injury from May 2025.
articles.body:
As the very early takeaways from the 2026-27 NBA season come pouring in, one thing people in the league are keeping an eye on is Jayson Tatum as he still rounds into form following his Achilles injury from May 2025.

An NBA scout who was in attendance for Tuesday's season-opening game between the Boston Celtics and Detroit Pistons told ESPN's Tim MacMahon they have questions about whether or not Tatum can be the "same guy" going forward:

"I do wonder if he's the same guy. Does he have the same burst and explosion? I'm not going to overreact to one game, but if the free throw numbers are down in December, that's an indication that he's not back to being himself coming off that Achilles. It's a telltale sign when guys are shooting jumpers instead of getting to the rim like they used to."

Tatum finished 6-of-23 (0-of-7 from three) with 13 points against the Pistons. Boston blew a 22-point lead, including allowing Detroit to go on a 23-0 run in the fourth quarter, in the 121-113 loss.

After tearing his Achilles in Game 4 of the Eastern Conference semfinals against the New York Knicks in May 2025, Tatum returned 10 months later. He has played in 23 games between the regular season and playoffs since returning.

Tatum is only shooting 40.9 percent from the field in those 23 games, down nearly five full percentage points from his career mark of 45.7. Another notable stat from this period is he is only averaging 4.7 free-throw attempts in 17 regular-season games, including one in the loss to Detroit.

In four seasons from 2021 to '25, Tatum never averaged fewer than 6.1 free-throw attempts per game.

The Celtics traded Jaylen Brown away in the offseason, likely betting on Tatum returning to being an MVP-caliber star to carry them. It's still very early in his return to make any sweeping judgements, but some of his statisical performance suggests he might be reluctant to play as aggressive as he did prior to the injury.

articles.title: Ole Miss MCBB Team Violates NCAA Tampering Rules, Full Punishment Announced
articles.summary: The NCAA has announced discipline against Mississippi men's basketball program stemming from tampering violations under former assistant coach Wes Flanigan.
articles.body:
The NCAA has announced discipline against Mississippi men's basketball program stemming from tampering violations under former assistant coach Wes Flanigan.

Per a release from the NCAA , the full list of penalties against Ole Miss includes a $455,000 fine and two years of probation:

A one-week ban on all recruiting communications for the men's basketball program, served during the 2025-26 academic year.

A one-week prohibition on unofficial and official visits for the men's basketball program, served during the 2024-25 academic year.

A one-week prohibition on all recruiting communications for Flanigan, served during the 2024-25 academic year.

A reduction by five in recruiting-person days for the men's basketball program served during the 2024-25 academic year.

A one-year show-cause order for Flanigan, including a suspension and recruiting communication restrictions. The suspension was served in December 2025 and recruiting restrictions were served in the 2024-25 academic year.

A two-game suspension for Flanigan, served from Dec. 13-17, 2025.

Disassociation of the booster for two years.

The athletics director and a senior member of the Ole Miss Athletic Foundation were required to attend the 2026 NCAA Regional Rules Seminar.

The release notes the case was resolved through the negotiated resolution process , which means the NCAA, school and individual parties involved agreed to "violation, level, classification and penalties" to reach a resolution.

Ole Miss head coach Chris Beard was deemed "automatically responsible for the violations due to head coach responsibility legislation," but wasn't directly disciplined since he wasn't directly involved in the violations and wasn't aware of the impermissible contact.

The violation stems from Flanigan's contact with the advisor of a student-athlete from another school who had not entered the transfer portal at the time.

Flanigan's contact with the advisor included 16 phone conversations and 10 text messages.

"In those communications, Flanigan and the advisor spoke about the student-athlete, but the student-athlete ― who subsequently was entered into the Transfer Portal ― did not visit Ole Miss, did not receive an offer of an athletics scholarship and ultimately transferred to another school," the NCAA wrote.

Flanigan spent three seasons as an assistant on Beard's staff at Ole Miss from 2023 to '26. The two previously worked together during the 2015-16 season when Beard was the head coach at Little Rock.

In April, Flanigan left Mississippi to take an associate head coach job at Georgia Tech under new head coach Scott Cross.

articles.title: WNBA players, coaches refuse to explain national anthem absences amid mounting criticism
articles.summary: Natalie Nakase and Gabby Williams cite a pregame routine for WNBA Finals anthem absences, while Rhyne Howard responds to criticism over Team USA.
articles.body: Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase called her team’s national anthem absences part of its pregame routine Friday, but did not explain who established that routine or why. OutKick had been trying to ask players and coaches about the anthem absences since Game 1. But after attending all 13 formal press conferences during the first three games without being called on, OutKick had to wait until Friday’s media availability ahead of Game 4 to ask those questions directly. "What do you do during those 90 seconds that you’re off the court?" OutKick asked. ATLANTA DREAM, GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES SKIP NATIONAL ANTHEM FOR THIRD STRAIGHT WNBA FINALS GAME "I’m with my staff, so I’m focused on my plays. That’s what I’m doing right now," Nakase responded. Golden State’s public relations staff then moved to the next reporter. OutKick did not get an opportunity to ask why those preparations needed to happen during the anthem, rather than before or afterward. The Valkyries and Atlanta Dream have been off the court during the national anthem before all three WNBA Finals games. In each game, players left shortly before the performance and returned seconds after it ended. Earlier in the exchange, OutKick had asked Nakase whose decision it was for the team to be absent and why it followed that routine. "We’re two years in," Nakase said. "That’s been part of our pregame." Asked again who decided and why, Nakase said, "I really don’t know." "I understand your question," she added. "I’m not trying to, you know, not answer your question. It’s just part of our pregame." Gabby Williams denies protest, cites longstanding routine Valkyries forward Gabby Williams was born in Nevada, holds U.S. and French citizenship and represents France in international competition. OutKick asked whether Golden State’s absence during the national anthem was a protest. "No," Williams said. Asked why the team was off the court during the U.S. national anthem, she responded: "That’s been the routine for like, seven years now." A Valkyries public relations representative then said, "Next question." Golden State is in its second season, and Williams joined the franchise this year. She played for Chicago from 2018–20 and Seattle from 2022–25, making the Valkyries the third WNBA team she has played for. Her seven-year reference would span her time with all three franchises, though she did not explain how the routine began or whether it was the same at each stop. VANCE CONDEMNS 'DISGRACEFUL' WNBA NATIONAL ANTHEM WALKOUTS, SAYS PLAYERS SHOULD SHOW MORE GRATITUDE There is a political history behind WNBA teams staying off the court during the anthem. During the 2017 Finals, Los Angeles Sparks players voted to remain in the locker room as a show of solidarity with the Black Lives Matter movement, according to ESPN’s reporting at the time. Atlanta also published players’ union messaging about anthem protests in its Aug. 2, 2020, game notes. The statement said "the anthem does not represent freedom, justice and liberty for all Americans" and that players would "continue to protest" in various forms. A protest can become a routine without ceasing to be a protest. Williams denied that Golden State’s absences are a demonstration, but saying the practice has lasted for years does not explain its purpose. Neither Williams nor Nakase explained who established Golden State’s routine or why it puts players off the court specifically during the anthem. Rhyne Howard responds to Team USA criticism Dream guard Rhyne Howard was asked about calls to exclude players from Team USA if they do not stand for the national anthem during the WNBA season. Riley Gaines and former Georgia state Rep. Vernon Jones have argued that athletes’ conduct during the anthem should carry consequences when they seek to represent the United States internationally. Howard represented the United States at September’s FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup, where she stood for the national anthem. "I mean, are we just talking about these three games or are we talking about the full season?" Howard asked. OutKick clarified that the question concerned both. "I don’t think I’ve been on the floor for the national anthem for any of my tenure in Atlanta, so if that’s what people are gonna look to nitpick for then so be it," Howard said. "But as far as competing for your team, when I go put on USA jersey I’m out for the national anthem every time, there’s no doubt about it." "Yes, I love the country that I play for and I love what we have here," she added. Howard also questioned the focus on the anthem during the WNBA Finals. OutKick followed up: "Is there a reason you’re not on the court for the anthem?" Howard and an Atlanta public relations representative both responded, "Next question." OutKick also sought to ask Angel Reese, Howard’s Dream and Team USA teammate, about the criticism. Most players and coaches were available throughout the 30-minute media window. Reese and Atlanta coach Karl Smesko were each required to be available for only 15 minutes. Reporters could jump in with questions during the other interviews Friday, but Atlanta public relations staff selected the questioners during Reese’s availability. OutKick was not called on and did not get an opportunity to ask her. Karl Smesko declines further comment on anthem Smesko was asked why his team had left the court shortly before each Finals anthem and returned shortly afterward, and whose decision that was. "We’re just kind of focused on the Finals," Smesko said. OutKick followed up by asking whether he had any comment on the anthem and his team’s absences on the league’s biggest stage. "No," Smesko said. An Atlanta public relations representative then moved the session to the next question. WNBA rulebook provision remains, but policy questions persist The WNBA’s 2026 official rulebook says players, coaches and trainers are to "stand and line up in a dignified posture" along the sidelines or on the foul line during the national anthem. The Associated Press reported Tuesday that the league suspended its anthem protocols in 2017. The provision remains in the 2026 rulebook, and OutKick has asked the WNBA to clarify its current requirements and enforcement. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD OutKick has also asked about possible discipline and exemptions, and sought comment from the NBA league office. The WNBA, NBA and both teams’ front offices have not responded to OutKick’s emailed requests for comment about the anthem absences. Friday’s responses came from players and coaches during media availabilities. The coaches and players have described a pregame routine that includes jogging off the court just prior to the national anthem and returning seconds after it ends. It's time for a new pregame routine.

articles.title: Dale Brown Dies at Age 90, Hall of Fame MCBB HC Led LSU to 2 Final Fours
articles.summary: LSU men's basketball head coach Dale Brown, who led the Tigers to the 1981 and 1986 Final Fours, four SEC titles, 13 NCAA tournament appearances and 448 wins during his 25 seasons at the helm, has died at the age of 90.
articles.body:
LSU men's basketball head coach Dale Brown, who led the Tigers to the 1981 and 1986 Final Fours, four SEC titles, 13 NCAA tournament appearances and 448 wins during his 25 seasons at the helm, has died at the age of 90.

LSU made the announcement on Friday. Brown's family released a statement as well.

"We have lost the most loving and most loved man any of us has ever known. Dale Brown always put others first. He always led with the heart. He was always a great humanitarian before anything else. Dale long ago fell in love with Louisiana. And the people of Louisiana loved him right back. We are forever grateful for that."

Ole Miss Men's CBB Punished for Violations

The university also released a video after news of his passing.

On Wednesday, Brown was named the 2027 recipient of the Los Angeles Athletic Club John R. Wooden Legends of Coaching Award.

Basketball Hall of Famer, NBA legend and ex-LSU star Shaquille O'Neal offered a message to his beloved coach after news of the award broke.

"He made me one of the best basketball players ever," O'Neal said in part. "Daddy Dale — we call you 'Daddy' for a reason. I love you and congratulations. I am so proud of you, Coach."

Brown coached O'Neal from 1989-1992 before the big man went to the NBA and enjoyed an illustrious career. Their relationship was covered extensively in the 2015 SEC Storied documentary, " Shaq and Dale ."

Per Gray Louisiana of FOX 8 WVUE-TV, Brown initially met O'Neal while leading a basketball clinic at a West Germany military base in 1984. Their relationship grew from there, and O'Neal eventually joined LSU a few years later.

O'Neal spoke with Khalid Salaam of Esquire in 2015 about what Brown meant to him.

"Away from the court he's a father figure, leader, and a motivator. His coaching style is one of belief, it wasn't all about plays all the time, it's about belief that you can get things done. When I was there we played some big games. We beat Arizona when they were No. 1, we beat Loyola Marymount, beat UNLV, lost to Duke twice. It wasn't about execution, it was about his speeches. I only ever played for two other coaches like that, and that's Phil Jackson and Pat Riley."

In addition to O'Neal, Brown coached numerous NBA players, including Mahmoud Abdul-Rauf, Jerry Reynolds, John Williams and Rudy Macklin.

On the court, Brown turned around a program that fell on hard times. From 1954-1972, LSU only had four winning seasons. LSU barely got there in three of them, going two games over .500 in that trio of campaigns.

Brown turned the team around, though. The Tigers notably went 31-5 (17-1 in SEC) in 1980-81 and made the Final Four. That LSU team ran off a 26-game winning streak during the regular season.

Brown's 1985-86 LSU team was the first-ever double-digit seed to make the Final Four. The No. 11 seed scored an upset over No. 1 Kentucky in the Elite Eight to earn the distinction.

Brown stands as the winningest coach in LSU men's hoops history. He was also second on the SEC list behind Kentucky's Adolph Rupp when he retired in 1997.

articles.title: 'Weakest S--t Ever,' Draymond Green Calls Out Technical Foul from Yaxel Lendeborg-Luka Doncic Spat
articles.summary: Draymond Green is defending Yaxel Lendeborg after the Golden State Warriors rookie received a technical foul late in the second quarter for trash-talking Luka Dončić during the Los Angeles Lakers' 127-105 win on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Draymond Green is defending Yaxel Lendeborg after the Golden State Warriors rookie received a technical foul late in the second quarter for trash-talking Luka Dončić during the Los Angeles Lakers' 127-105 win on Wednesday night.

On the latest episode of his podcast (starts at 4:25 mark), Green called it the "weakest s--t ever" when discussing Landeborg's technical foul.

"The whole world saw them jawing back and forth. For Yaxel to get a tech for saying something on one play that Luka doesn't say something, I thought was the weakest shit ever. I thought that was pathetic. When a guy is mixing it up with a guy and a rookie is not backing down, you don't punish the rookie with a technical foul because he's not backing down from the superstar. There's enough rookies that back down from superstars. But it's like, get in line. No, you shut up. Why, because he's a rookie, should he shut up? Why? I came in talking. When I hit my game-winner against the Miami Heat as a rookie, me and Bron were already talking, mixing it up. He tells me I'm too little, I score to tell him he's too little, then I get the walk-off. That was, guess what, when you see the respect and love that Bron and I have for each other now, it starts there, from a guy not backing down."

The foul was assessed with 22 seconds remaining in the second quarter. Landeborg and Dončić had been jawing for a bit, then Landeborg kept it going as he was walking up the floor after the Warriors regained possession.

On a night when the Lakers easily defeated Golden State with Dončić, Austin Reaves and Walker Kessler combining for 77 of Los Angeles' 127 points, the biggest story coming out of it was Landeborg's comments about Dončić.

Landeborg ripped the Lakers superstar for "complaining the entire game" and that he "lost all respect" for him. He also revealed he told Dončić "he sucks" at one point during the game when they were trash-talking each other.

Dončić immediately responded after the technical foul by hitting a half-court three as time expired in the first half.

Warriors head coach Steve Kerr told reporters after the game he appreciated Landeborg's "bravado" against Dončić, but did add "don't foul him next time … back up your words."

It was certainly a notable debut for Landeborg, though not for reasons anyone was expecting. The 24-year-old will be relied on heavily by the Warriors, especially with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody out with injuries, so his confidence will serve him well going forward.

Landeborg and the Warriors will look to bounce back on Friday night when they host the Memphis Grizzlies at Chase Center.

articles.title: Fever Fire GM Amber Cox After Team President Kelly Krauskopf Steps Down
articles.summary: Ahead of one of the most important offseasons in franchise history, the Indiana Fever's front office is undergoing significant changes.
articles.body:
Ahead of one of the most important offseasons in franchise history, the Indiana Fever's front office is undergoing significant changes.

The Fever have fired general manager Amber Cox, they announced Friday. The Athletic's Annie Costabile was first to report the news.

The move comes after the Fever announced on Friday morning that Kelly Krauskopf is stepping down from her role as team president.

Despite their first-round exit this season, the Fever set a franchise record with 28 wins during the regular season. Their .636 winning percentage was the third-best in franchise history after 2009 and 2012.

Indiana's decision to move on from Cox comes as the team enters a crucial offseason.

Kelsey Mitchell is set to hit free agency coming off a historic 2026 in which she averaged a career-high 24.7 points per game, setting WNBA records for most total points in a season and most consecutive 20-point games.

Mitchell admitted in her end-of-season press conference she will be "selfish" when it comes to negotiating her next contract, while also mentioning some of "ups and downs" about playing for the Fever:

"But I think, ultimately, being on the Fever and being a part of an organization that does come with a lot of ups and downs, what factors in and what is important for me is, obviously, having a good chemistry on and off the floor. I've only been with one team my entire career, so it's all kind of like figuring this out. It's hard, man."

Sophie Cunningham is the other notable Fever player who will become a free agent. Caitlin Clark is eligible to sign an extension off her rookie contract, which is set to expire after the 2027 season.

Cox just wrapped up her second season with Indiana after being hired in October 2024. She held the titles of general manager and chief operating officer.

The Fever went 52-36 and made the playoffs twice under Cox, but their lone postseason series victory was in the first round against the Atlanta Dream in 2025. They have been eliminated by the Las Vegas Aces in both years.

Cox was the fourth different general manager for the Fever since 2018. Krauskopf, who held the title from 2004 to '17, is the only person who has been Indiana's GM for more than four seasons since the franchise was founded in 2000.

articles.title: Knicks call plan to use fake championship rings as employee phishing test 'an unfortunate mistake,' will issue rings to employees
articles.summary: A spokesperson said the organization will be giving rings and jewelry to players, coaches and employees after report of the cybersecurity test went public.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks appear to be pivoting after a report that the team used the promise of championship rings as a cybersecurity test . In a statement to Yahoo Sports on Friday, a spokesperson for Madison Square Garden (MSG) confirmed a report from The Athletic that the company had sent emails last month offering employees championship rings as a phishing test.

The company said it had recently undergone a hack, which led to the test, likely under the urging of Knicks owner James Dolan, who is known to be worried about cybersecurity.

"The company had previously sent out an email to its corporate team as a simulation of a phishing attack designed to strengthen our security against hackers," the spokesman said. "MSG was recently hacked and extorted using an employee login and password obtained through a similar phishing attack. Using the rings as a lure to gain employees attention was an unfortunate mistake."

Part of the oddness of the targeted phishing test is that, as The Athletic reported, many longtime MSG employees were not going to be receiving rings at all. That includes some who work in the Knicks' business operations — a role that would typically result in receiving a ring.

The Knicks also appear to be walking that back as well: The spokesman told Yahoo Sports that the company will be giving "more than 275 championship rings and jewelry to players, coaches, employees and other members of the Knicks family." The jewelry will total more than $3.7 million, per the company.

Individual teams typically get to decide who, in addition to the players, will receive rings after a championship, but many owners will give out more simple versions of the players' rings to employees within the organization.

Knicks players received their massive, diamond-encrusted rings during the team's home opener on Tuesday, with the championship banner also getting raised into the rafters at MSG. The rings feature a removable top that reveals a miniature Madison Square Garden.

articles.title: Indiana Fever fires GM Amber Cox in another front-office shakeup
articles.summary: The move comes shortly after president Kelly Krauskopf announced that she is stepping down, as the Fever take stock after a disappointing first-round exit in...
articles.body:
Indiana Fever chief operating officer and general manager Amber Cox has been fired. The team announced her "departure" on Friday, confirming multiple reports.

"Through her two seasons with the Fever, Amber has helped us navigate the seismic growth of both the WNBA and our franchise," Mel Raines, president and CEO of Pacers Sports and Entertainment (PS&E) said in a statement from the team. "We're grateful for her contributions and wish her the very best moving forward."

Cox's ouster marks the second front-office shakeup of the day, after team president Kelly Krauskopf announced she would be stepping down from her position.

Cox was hired as the team's COO and GM in October 2024 after two years as the COO of the Dallas Wings. Prior to her time with the Wings, Cox served as the vice president for sports with the Connecticut Sun from 2016 to 2021.

Krauskopf, who has been part of PS&E since 1999, was reportedly directly involved in Cox's hire.

The front-office shakeup comes at a crucial time for the Fever, after Indiana was dispatched in the first round of the WNBA playoffs with a loss to the Las Vegas Aces. Indiana was already facing questions this offseason , but the search for a new president and GM will now take center stage.

Another offseason question was whether head coach Stephanie White would be staying with the team. In her postseason availability, Cox had said that the "continuity" of keeping White on board was something to keep in consideration.

"I think the expectation is always championship. We didn't meet that expectation, but we're going to learn from it and we're going to grow. Steph's players know that she rides for them," Cox said.

For now, though, White will be staying with the team, while Cox's time has come to an end.

Star guard Kelsey Mitchell, who led the team in scoring and was the second-highest scorer in the WNBA this season, is a free agent after coming off a one-year deal, while Sophie Cunningham is also a free agent. Aliyah Boston, another star player, underwent knee surgery after the postseason loss and has an unclear return timeline.

articles.title: Draymond Green Says 'Greatness Fatigue' Will Prevent Lakers' Luka Doncic from Winning NBA MVP
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green said "greatness fatigue" will prevent Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Dončić from winning an NBA MVP.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green said "greatness fatigue" will prevent Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Dončić from winning an NBA MVP.

"Nah, I don't think there's anything that he can do (to win it)," Green told Sam Amick of The Athletic after Dončić posted 28 points, eight rebounds, seven assists and three steals in 30 minutes in the Lakers' season-opening win over the 127-105 win over the Warriors on Wednesday.

"And by the way, it's not a knock on him. I don't think there is anything that he can do. If they're the 1, 2, 3 seed — great. It's still Luka Dončić. No one is going to be surprised that Luka Dončić's team is the 4 seed. Nobody. He's that good. There's no element of surprise if his team is the fourth seed.

Bold Predictions for 2026-27 NBA Season 🔮

"I just think, ultimately, he gets screwed because of it. And it's probably a little unfair. Anybody else puts those numbers up, and they're walking away with the MVP. Like, home free. That's why I made the comparison to Bron. He's got, what, four MVPs? You're telling me he wasn't the best player in the NBA for at least 10 seasons? It's greatness fatigue."

As Amick noted, Dončić didn't receive a vote from any of the league's 30 general managers in the latest annual NBA GM Survey in response to a question about who would win MVP.

San Antonio Spurs big man Victor Wembanyama got 23 votes. Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokić received three, Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander took two, and Minnesota Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards and Boston Celtics forward Jayson Tatum received one apiece.

Lakers wing Austin Reaves had this to say regarding the results and Green's remarks.

"You can go ask any of those GMs if they want him on their team, and they're going to take him," Reaves told Amick. "There's a lot of truth in what (Green) said. Luka has done what he's done for eight years now, and when he does it, there's no wow factor.

"There's a wow factor when he plays, but you look at the box (score) after the game, and you're like … 'Oh, he had 35 (points).' So when he has 40, people aren't like, 'Holy s—, he had 40!' It's like, 'Oh, he did what he does every single night.' So, I think there's a little bit of truth in what Draymond said about voter fatigue with someone who hasn't won it."

Six of the last seven seasons have resulted in Dončić making the All-NBA First Team. The only exception was 2024-25, when Dončić was limited to 50 games due to injury.

Dončić has been great to say the least, although he hasn't been close to winning the MVP. His best MVP race result was third in 2023-24, when Dončić (then a member of the eventual Western Conference champion Dallas Mavericks) averaged an NBA-high 33.9 PPG.

Dončić received four of a possible 100 first-place votes. Denver Nuggets big man Nikola Jokić earned 79 first-place votes en route to winning the MVP easily.

From 2019-20 through 2025-26, Dončić has averaged 30.5 points, 8.6 rebounds, 8.6 assists and 1.5 steals per game. Needless to say, those are incredible numbers, especially over a seven-season span. There's no doubt he's one of the NBA's elite players and deserves MVP consideration every year.

The problem is that he has faced great competition in the MVP race (Jokić, Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, a breakout year from Philadelphia 76ers big man Joel Embiid). Wembanyama has joined the MVP conversation as well.

In addition, Dončić's teams have never been atop (or near the top) of the Western Conference in the regular season, topping out at fourth. That might be an issue again this year with the Thunder and San Antonio Spurs, on paper, looking like two powerhouses who should pace the West.

To Green's point, "greatness fatigue" is certainly possible. Dončić puts up huge stats and the team's offense on his back every night. It's what he does, to the point where perhaps people can fall into the trap of taking it for granted.

Ultimately, Dončić has bigger issues than the MVP, and that's trying to lead the Lakers to its first title since 2020. They got off to a good start Wednesday as the new-look squad fired on all cylinders in a 22-point win.

articles.title: Mark Walter reportedly looking to sell WNBA's Sparks after Lakers, Chelsea sales
articles.summary: Walter's camp has been insistent the Dodgers aren't for sale.
articles.body:
Mark Walter appears ready to part with another piece of his sports empire, which has been crumbling for months.

After selling his majority stake in the NBA's Los Angeles Lakers and his minority stake in Chelsea of the Premier League , the billionaire is seeking a sale of the WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks according to Bloomberg .

Walter is reportedly looking to sell the Sparks and their team facility for at least $700 million, which would shatter the record for the most expensive sale in WNBA history. That title currently belongs to the $300 million the Fertitta family paid for the Connecticut Sun, which is being relocated to Houston .

The most recent round of Sportico team valuations estimated the Sparks' value at $400 million, though such projections often differ from the team's actual price. Sportico's NBA values were more than a billion dollars below both the $10 billion valuation Walter paid to acquire the Lakers, then the $12.5 billion he got from Bob Iger and Joshua Kushner.

Walter has owned a majority stake in the Sparks in 2014, two years after his Guggenheim Partners consortium purchased the Los Angeles Dodgers. Like with the Dodgers, Walter has counted Magic Johnson, Todd Boehly, Robert Patton and Stan Kasten among his Sparks co-owners.

Walter's reaction has been to raise as much cash as possible in order to pay off those deals under investigation, hence his deals with the Lakers, Chelsea and now potentially the Sparks.

From a sports perspective, the question remains whether Walter will be forced to sell the Dodgers, which have become the powerhouse of MLB with record payrolls, three World Series titles and 13 NL West titles under his ownership.

Both Kasten, the president of the Dodgers, and Walter's TWG Global firm have been insistent the Dodgers are not for sale.

In addition to the Dodgers and Sparks, Walter also owns the Professional Women's Hockey League the Cadillac F1 racing team and IndyCar's Andretti Global team.

articles.title: Rui Hachimura looking forward to playing on other side of Lakers-Clippers rivalry
articles.summary: After playing the last three-plus seasons with the Lakers, Rui Hachimura will suit up against them for the Clippers.
articles.body:
Rui Hachimura is now in his fifth NBA season in Los Angeles but returns to Crypto.com Arena wearing a different uniform.

He spent the past three-plus seasons with the Los Angeles Lakers before signing with the L.A. Clippers as a free agent during the offseason. The Lakers and Clippers play Friday night.

"I'm looking forward to it," Hachimura said Wednesday after the Clippers' season-opening win over the Sacramento Kings. "I'm going to see all my old teammates and coaches. Playing in that arena is special. I'm excited."

The former Gonzaga basketball player signed a two-year deal with the Clippers worth $28 million.

"I'm excited to see the fans," Hachimura said. "I love them. It's a special game but we got to get the win."

Hachimura nearly produced a double-double in his debut with the Clippers. He finished with 10 points, eight rebounds and two assists in 23 minutes of play as a starter.

Rui Hachimura on Friday's game vs. Lakers

Hachimura spent the first three-plus seasons of his career with the Washington Wizards before he was traded to the Lakers in January 2023.

The Japanese player started nine of the 33 games he played for the Lakers that season. He earned a key role in the rotation.

He averaged 45 starts per season during his final three seasons with the Lakers. He averaged 12.3 points and 4.3 rebounds during his tenure with the Lakers, shooting 41.5% from the 3-point line.

Lakers coach JJ Redick knows what kind of person Hachimura is after two seasons as his coach, and he knows what kind of threat Hachimura will be as an opposing player now.

"In terms of his offensive packaging, he's one of the best shooters in the NBA," Redick told reporters this week. "We got him at a good point in his career. ... His mid-range game is great.

"He's one of my favorite players I've ever been around in the NBA and one of my favorite players that I've ever coached and it's because of the consistency of joy and personality that he brings every day."

Lakers standout Austin Reaves shared a similar sentiment about Hachimaura and described his initial reaction to him.

"He's an unbelievable human, but I didn't know if he spoke English for the first two weeks," Reaves told reporters. "I would sit by him on the plane and he didn't speak to me and then after that I couldn't get him to shut up, but he's a great guy and a great player and I miss him."

The Clippers will visit the Lakers Friday for a Pacific Division game at Crypto.com Arena. Tip-off should come shortly after 7 p.m. PT.

articles.title: Alpha Diallo Could Be a Difference-Maker for the Nuggets
articles.summary: On July 12, the Denver Nuggets made a very interesting signing, bringing in 29-year-old rookie Alpha Diallo from the EuroLeague on a one-year, $1.4 million d...
articles.body:
On July 12, the Denver Nuggets made a very interesting signing, bringing in 29-year-old rookie Alpha Diallo from the EuroLeague on a one-year, $1.4 million deal. At first, this move may seem insignificant, as few expect him to get much playing time. Most see it as a way for Denver to just round out their roster, but Diallo could end up being a pivotal addition for the Nuggets.

For those who haven't heard of him, Alpha Diallo is a 6-foot-7 wing, who played four years of college ball at Providence, where he was named two-time Second-team All-Big East. After going undrafted in 2020, he played one year for Lavrio B.C. in the Greek league. Afterward, he joined French club AS Monaco, where he played from 2021 until 2026.

Across his five years in Europe, Diallo achieved tremendous success, both individually and with his team. He won the French league championship three times with Monaco. Additionally, Diallo earned league first-team honors twice and second-team honors twice while also being a two-time winner of the Best Defender award.

Despite his success in the French league, Diallo still had not grasped the attention of NBA executives. Last season, he was able to do just that. In the EuroLeague, where all of Europe's best teams play, Diallo won the Best Defender award while leading the league in steals.

Diallo's stats may not jump off the page. He only averaged about 10 points per game; he was a streaky shooter from three, and he wasn't racking up assists or rebounds. However, this is not uncommon in European leagues, as the numbers seldom translate. In the French league, even superstar Victor Wembanyama only averaged over 9.4 points per game in one season. Even Luka Doncic never averaged over 16 points per game for Real Madrid.

The NBA has plenty of scorers. The best way for an NBA hopeful to earn a place in the league is to be a winner and a challenging defender. With his three league championships and Best Defender awards, Diallo embodies exactly that.

The NBA is very different from the European leagues. Naturally, fans may wonder if Diallo will be able to hack it. Granted, the sample size for veterans coming from Europe to the NBA is small, and frankly unimpressive. However, Diallo has all the makings to be the exception. Thankfully for him, defense is one attribute of basketball that is universal.

Oftentimes, Defensive Player of the Year awards are won by guards or bigs, not wings. Diallo was the first wing to win the EuroLeague DPOY award since 2017. Expanding upon that notion, only one wing has won the two collegiate awards, the Naismith DPOY and NABC DPOY , respectively, since its inception in 2018. Those two wings were Matisse Thybulle and De'Andre Hunter, who have both carved out solid NBA careers.

The last wing to win the NBA DPOY was Kawhi Leonard in 2016. Simply put, for a wing to win the award, regardless of the league, they truly must be a special defender.

Something else the Nuggets had to consider when signing him was Diallo's age. Some may view it as a detriment, believing he has already peaked. But it may prove to be an advantage. The Nuggets are a veteran team contending for a championship. The last thing they need is an inexperienced youngster whom they have to develop. Diallo is a veteran and a proven winner who can fit seamlessly on the squad and mesh with the team culture.

Admittedly, there are likely plenty of NBA teams where Diallo would not be immediately getting opportunities. Denver is a perfect landing spot for him.

Despite being first in offensive rating last season, the Nuggets struggled defensively, finishing outside the top 20 . Their poor defense played a massive role in their embarrassing first-round loss to the undermanned Timberwolves. With his defensive prowess, coach David Adelman will surely find ways to get Diallo on the court to supplement their woes.

Diallo's prospective opportunities on the court extend beyond just defensive needs. The Nuggets have a serious depth issue at the wing position. Of their starting wings, Christian Braun completely under-performed while new acquisition, Cameron Johnson , had some disappointing stretches. Denver somewhat addressed the issue by bringing in six-time All-Star DeMar DeRozan , but that's about all they did this offseason.

While DeRozan and Spencer Jones have two of the five bench spots locked up, the rest are somewhat up for grabs. Granted, Diallo will likely not be getting reps at point guard or center, but the opportunity remains.

Additionally, Julian Strawther , who was expected to start the year as the backup shooting guard, will be sidelined with a knee injury until December. Thus, with poor wing depth, defensive concerns, and an opening at the position, the Nuggets almost have to give Diallo a decent role to start the year.

The returns in Diallo's first game with the Nuggets were good as far as his role goes. He played a total of 22 minutes off the bench, scoring four points on 2-of-4 from the field. He was a +1 in the Nuggets' 12-point loss to the Thunder.

However, with a strong starting lineup and key bench guys like DeRozan and Jones, 20 minutes per game for him seems like his ceiling over the course of the full season.

Nevertheless, he truly could establish himself as a useful bench piece. For instance, Jones was virtually unknown at the start of last year. Through rough defense, hustle, and an efficient three-ball, he became invaluable for Denver. Diallo could follow a similar path.

The defense and hustle are absolutely there. The main question about Diallo revolves around his shooting. He hasn't been very consistent, but he has shown flashes, shooting over 40% in the EuroLeague in 2024 and 2025.

On paper, Diallo is a perfect fit for Denver. They desperately need better wing defenders, and they got a great one for under $2 million. Playing great defense truly is the best way to earn minutes. If he can defend in the NBA at a high level and his shot starts falling, he'll be hard to keep off the court. Few know his name right now, but that may not be the case by the end of the season.
